text:
aisha (CSM): dropping a tiny, copy-paste friendly set of customer-facing checks for the first 0-14 days. goal: reduce churn by catching streaming/batching cache misconfig early :seedling:

maria (CS Ops): love it. short + actionable = win. can you include a single one-page checklist we can paste into kickoff emails?

aisha (CSM): yes — below is the one-pager we tested last week. it's intentionally terse so customers actually read it. feel free to copy into enablement docs.

---
Customer Quick-Check: First 0-14 days (paste into kickoff)
1) Account health: confirm routing + keys
   - Verify API key in the Console -> "Keys" matches your integration.
   - Confirm region used (us-west / eu-central) to avoid cross-region latency.
2) Traffic & latency baseline (first 48h)
   - Run simple throughput test: 10 reqs/s for 5 min, record p50/p95 latency.
   - If p95 > 750ms for chat gen, toggle to smaller batch size or enable prefix cache.
3) Caching sanity
   - Recommended: enable prefix caching for stable prompts (10-15s TTL to start).
   - Validate with: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/cache/check -d '{"key":"example-user-flow"}'
4) Batching guidance
   - Begin with conservative batch sizes: 8 seqs for small models, 4 for long-context.
   - If you see latency spikes, reduce batch size and enable jittered backoff client-side.
5) Streaming checks
   - Test stream fallbacks: confirm client can handle final-token-only responses.
   - Sample: websocket handshake + event order MUST tolerate out-of-order reconnects.
6) Renewal risk signals (early flags)
   - >3 days of rising p95 or >15% user drop in session length → flag AHT review.
   - Capture feedback: one-question in-app survey after first 5 sessions.
7) Escalation matrix
   - CS first line: reply in <4h for live accounts.
   - Engineering triage: escalate to @jamie if rollout/batch tuning needed.
---

jamie (Eng): small addition — include this sample for measuring tokens & cost per request so customers can plan renewals: 

```bash
# quick token estimate (client-side)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/estimate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-7b","input":"<user prompt here>"}'
```

eli (SRE): ops note: if a customer enables aggressive batching, set a soft limit on burst queueing. we recommend queue-depth <= 250 per tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor latencies. ops-bot will attach alerts if queue depth > 200 for 10m.

ops-bot: Alert rule created: queue.depth.tenant > 200 for 10m -> channel #eng-oncall, cc @eli (SRE) :bell:

maria (CS Ops): also adding a tiny script snippet customers can run to verify streaming integrity (reconnect tolerant):

```python
# reconnect-tolerant stream consumer (pseudo)
import websocket, time
while True:
  try:
    ws = websocket.create_connection('wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1/stream?key=$KEY')
    for msg in ws:
      handle(msg)
  except Exception:
    time.sleep(1 + random.random())  # jittered backoff
    continue
```

aisha (CSM): perfect. last thing — quick customer-facing phrasing for the renewal playbook: "If latency or accuracy regress for more than 72h, we'll open a joint investigation and propose short-term routing to a compatible variant while we fix the root cause."

jamie (Eng): that phrasing is good — add optional step: canary to warmed dedicated pool for heavy customers.

maria (CS Ops): I'll paste this into the shared enablement snippet library and link it in the next kickoff template.

aisha (CSM): awesome. i'll run a/b test with two customers next week and report flags back here. thanks team :rocket:
